summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, diaphoresis, cough, and altered mental status, and found to have presumed pneumonia, for which he was initially managed in the ICU before transfer to the floor. During his stay, he developed left hand cellulitis, likely related to IV access, which was treated with antibiotics after MRI confirmation. He was diagnosed with Clostridioides difficile infection, requiring a 14-day course of oral vancomycin. Transaminitis developed, possibly medication-related or due to underlying hepatitis B, prompting discontinuation of meropenem; liver enzymes subsequently improved. His multiple myeloma remained stable, though chemotherapy was held due to infection and cytopenias. He recovered well, with resolution of infections and improvement in symptoms, and was discharged home with follow-up plans and a full medication regimen.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of hand, except fingers and thumb
